text:
Ophelia has 20 sofas, and she has 2 fewer sofas than chairs, so she has $20 + 2 = 22$ chairs.
Jenna has 3 times as many chairs as Ophelia, so she has $3 \times 22 = 66$ chairs.
Jenna also has 2 fewer sofas than chairs, so she has $66 - 2 = 64$ sofas.

The total number of sofas and chairs is:
$20 + 22 + 64 + 66 = 172$

ANSWER: 172
